text:
Vladislav Gavrikov is the Rangers' quiet defenseman, a sixth-round pick from 2015 playing 21 and a half minutes a night in his second season in New York after Columbus and Los Angeles. He has seven points in 21 games and has blocked 40 shots, and his value isn't in the box score.

The underlying play has been solid. The Rangers take 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Gavrikov on the ice, 3.5 points better than without him, and the goal results are fair, with no luck to give back. His one goal matches his expected total. Last season he scored 14 goals, and our talent range expects closer to 7 this time.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level by results last season, but better by chance quality: the finishing and the goaltending behind him let him down. With Sean Durzi out and Adam Fox carrying more minutes, Gavrikov's pairing has to hold up against the other team's top lines, and so far it has. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking doesn't find a standout strength or weakness, which suits a defenseman whose job is to make nothing happen.
